# AI Disclosures Project

These notes restate public material from the AI Disclosures Project: its website, its GitHub organization and the Open Memory Protocol repository, read on 2026-10-22. Each note keeps its source URL.

Start with [the project](project/ai-disclosures-project.md), [the Open Memory Protocol](omp/what-is-omp.md), [the memory record](spec/memory-object.md), [the open issues](spec/open-issues.md) and [the Asimov’s Addendum blog](blog/asimovs-addendum.md). Notes about Ilan himself are under [personal](personal/ilan.md).
title: AI Disclosures Project

body:
# The AI Disclosures Project

The AI Disclosures Project works on market-shaping protocols, technical standards and economic mechanisms so that value circulates broadly rather than being trapped inside a handful of gatekeepers. It works through research, prototypes and convenings. It is hosted at [Code for Science & Society](fiscal-home.md), and its site names Omidyar Network as a funder. It is led by [Tim O’Reilly and Ilan Strauss](../people/directors.md), who also write [Asimov’s Addendum](../blog/asimovs-addendum.md).
title: The AI Disclosures Project

body:
# Hosted at Code for Science & Society

The AI Disclosures Project is a project of Code for Science & Society (CS&S), a registered 501(c)(3) public charity. [OMPI](../ompi/initiative.md) is a named initiative housed there; no new legal entity is created during the grant period. CS&S and the project keep the fiduciary, employment, contracting and grant-accountability duties.
title: Hosted at Code for Science & Society

body:
# The project on GitHub

The GitHub organization The-AI-Disclosures-Project hosts the Open-Memory-Protocol repository (created 2026-08-26), follow_up_research, and code for three papers: detecting access violations in LLM pre-training data, ecosystem exploitation in search results, and real-world gaps in AI governance research. See [research](../research/attribution-and-access.md).
title: The project on GitHub

body:
# Tim O’Reilly and Ilan Strauss direct the project

Tim O’Reilly is founder and co-director (and founder and CEO of O’Reilly Media). Ilan Strauss is co-director. Strauss also lists roles as an honorary senior fellow at UCL IIPP, a senior fellow at the Microsoft AI Economy Institute, a visiting associate professor at the University of Johannesburg, and a member of the Data & Policy editorial board. See also [the team](team.md) and [Ilan’s profile](../personal/ilan.md).
title: Tim O’Reilly and Ilan Strauss direct the project

body:
# Researchers, scholars and advisors

Sruly Rosenblat is the project’s technical researcher. Affiliated scholars are Rufus Rock (CMU) and Jangho Yang (University of Waterloo). The advisory committee is Anna Tumadóttir (Creative Commons), Erika Augustine (The David Prize), Daniel Goroff (ex officio, Sloan Foundation), Tim O’Reilly and Ilan Strauss. Leadership: [directors](directors.md).
title: Researchers, scholars and advisors

body:
# Protocols and Power (August 2025)

“Protocols and Power”, also published as “Open Protocols Can Prevent AI Monopolies”, is by M. Moure, T. O’Reilly and I. Strauss (August 2025). It argues that open protocols such as MCP keep AI context fluid and limit platform lock-in, and recommends authorized access to user-owned data and portable agent memory. The OMP README cites it as the case that started [the memory work](../omp/what-is-omp.md).
title: Protocols and Power (August 2025)

body:
# MCP in practice (August 2025)

“MCP In Practice” (S. Rosenblat, I. Strauss, T. O’Reilly and I. Moore, August 2025) analyzes 2,874 MCP servers and finds activity concentrated in a few high-use servers. It argues for open APIs, portable memory and transparent dependencies. Related: [Protocols and Power](protocols-and-power.md).
title: MCP in practice (August 2025)

body:
# The Memory Walled Garden (October 2025)

Published on 2025-10-03 in [Asimov’s Addendum](../blog/asimovs-addendum.md). Chat history is locked inside first-party apps: none of the five MCP memory servers surveyed could read ChatGPT or Claude history. It recommends that OpenAI and Anthropic expose memory through MCP or an API with OAuth. The OMP README calls it the ecosystem’s first public position on [portable agent memory](../omp/why-omp.md).
title: The Memory Walled Garden (October 2025)

body:
# Attribution and access research

“Beyond Public Access in LLM Pre-Training Data” (Rosenblat, O’Reilly, Strauss; April 2025) reports that GPT-4o shows signs of prior exposure to paywalled O’Reilly books. “The Attribution Crisis in LLM Search Results” (Strauss, Yang, O’Reilly, Rosenblat, Moure; Data & Policy) estimates ecosystem exploitation from about 14,000 LMArena logs. “Governing AI Through SEC Disclosure” is an SSRC policy report from October 2025.
title: Attribution and access research

body:
# Asimov’s Addendum, the blog

Asimov’s Addendum is a newsletter on Substack by Tim O’Reilly and Ilan Strauss. It considers what additional “laws” might be needed for AI, with a focus on disclosures as protocols and built-in software standards. Its tagline: “Participatory, decentralized AI markets built for human participation, reward, and oversight.” It runs parallel to research housed at the Social Science Research Council but is not affiliated with it. Posts: [summer 2026](summer-2026-posts.md), [August 2026](august-2026-posts.md), and [The Memory Walled Garden](../research/memory-walled-garden.md).
title: Asimov’s Addendum, the blog

body:
# The Open Memory Protocol

The Open Memory Protocol (OMP) is an open, royalty-free technology for portable, interoperable memory across AI agents and services. It is a transfer format, not a storage format: each tool keeps its own storage and implements one import and one export. Why it exists: [the problem](why-omp.md). Who develops it: [OMPI](../ompi/initiative.md).
title: The Open Memory Protocol

body:
# Why agent memory needs a shared format

Each coding harness (Claude Code, Codex, goose, OpenClaw, Letta Code) keeps memory in its own conventions: AGENTS.md, MEMORY.md, USER.md, HUMAN.md. Agents can’t move between harnesses, and provenance and permissions are lost on export. The first vertical is coding agents; see the [roadmap](roadmap.md).
title: Why agent memory needs a shared format

body:
# OMP roadmap

Year 1 (2026–27): lock the schema and exchange semantics, and have two harnesses ship conformant export and import. Year 2 (2027–28): a transport layer and extensions. The scoping note names five shared practices to standardize: persistence across sessions, scope and ownership, lifecycle operations, selective retrieval, and controls and policy.
title: OMP roadmap

body:
# How the memory work unfolded

August 2025: [Protocols and Power](../research/protocols-and-power.md). October 2025: [the Walled Garden post](../research/memory-walled-garden.md). May 2026: first commits on an ACP memory-server prototype. June 2026: a FOO Camp session. August 2026: Charles Packer circulates a draft spec. 2026-09-09: first online convening, co-hosted with Mozilla and IBM. October 2026: an in-person gathering in Berkeley.
title: How the memory work unfolded

body:
# OMPI and its partners

The Open Memory Protocol Initiative (OMPI) is the multi-stakeholder, vendor-neutral ecosystem that develops OMP, housed at the AI Disclosures Project. Mozilla and IBM are in-kind partners and co-hosts. Letta is a spec author and reference implementer; Block’s goose is the first-vertical implementer. Proposals also came from Cognee, Context Nest and the Mila + Mozilla AMS Card. Governance: [steering group](governance.md).
title: OMPI and its partners

body:
# OMPI governance

A Technical Steering Group holds in-kind partner seats (Mozilla, IBM), a spec-author seat (Letta) and rotating working-group seats. Breaking changes need a two-thirds vote and a migration plan. No funder, sponsor or founding organization gets a technical veto. Specs and docs are CC BY 4.0, code is Apache 2.0, and contributions use a DCO sign-off. See [how to join](how-to-join.md).
title: OMPI governance

body:
# How to take part in OMPI

Open issues and pull requests against the drafts, or run the Python loader and validator prototype. The Discord is by application, and the address is ompi@aidisclosures.org. The working group meets monthly, on the second Tuesday at 10:00 ET. Protocol changes need an issue with at least two weeks of public discussion.
title: How to take part in OMPI

body:
# The working spec is the v0.1 draft

The OMPI page lists the AI Disclosures Project draft spec v0.1 as the working specification. It is open for review, not an adopted standard.
title: The working spec is the v0.1 draft

body:
# The working spec is the v0.2 editors’ draft

The working specification is the v0.2 editors’ draft of 2026-10-14 (PR #13), renamed from v0.1. It defines [the memory object](memory-object.md). It folds in reviews from IBM, the AI Disclosures Project and a technical working meeting. It is an editors’ draft, not an adopted standard; the OMPI page still lists v0.1.
title: The working spec is the v0.2 editors’ draft

links.reason: PR #13 replaced the v0.1 working draft with the v0.2 editors’ draft on 2026-10-14.

body:
# The OMP memory object

A memory is metadata plus a body; Markdown is neither required nor preferred. Records carry an `identifier` and a `media_type`, with optional `path`, `title`, `tags`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, `updated_at`, `provenance`, `evidence` and `links`. The audit profile adds `version` and `checksum`. Who said it: [provenance](provenance.md). How exports travel: [manifest](manifest-and-receipts.md).
title: The OMP memory object

body:
# Provenance: who said it

`provenance` is a list of contributors, each with an `id`, a `kind` (human, agent or system) and a `contribution`. A missing provenance means author unknown, and must not be read as the user’s own words. The editors propose no portable accuracy score; confidence travels as contributions such as verified or contradicted, plus evidence (issue I-20).
title: Provenance: who said it

body:
# Manifest, receipts and import rules

An export’s manifest declares the protocol version, profiles, `origin` (with `identifier`, the global key), when it was exported and whether it is a snapshot, a selection or full history. Each export declares an intent: copy, move or federation. Import receipts mark each memory accepted, transformed, omitted or rejected. Dangling links are kept and marked, and credentials are never exported. Forgetting: [tombstones](forgetting.md).
title: Manifest, receipts and import rules

body:
# Forgetting and tombstones

A forget erases content but leaves a tombstone recording when, who and why, never the content. Receivers must not restore forgotten content from older archives (anti-resurrection). The editors propose putting this in the audit profile; that is open issue I-7 in [the open issues](open-issues.md).
title: Forgetting and tombstones

body:
# Open issues in the v0.2 draft

I-5 links (inline or metadata edges). I-7 tombstones and anti-resurrection: core or audit? I-8 identity on import. I-19 folders beyond `path`. I-20 accuracy as provenance plus evidence, or a field. I-21 a thin core with separately versioned semantic conventions, Ilan’s proposal. I-22 trust and sanitization of imported memories. Related pull requests: [open PRs](open-prs.md).
title: Open issues in the v0.2 draft

body:
# Proposals under review

PR #16 (Cognee) adds origin, invalidated_by, a body-only content hash, evidence with confidence, and accuracy. PR #17 is a threat model that separates integrity from trustworthiness and proposes making anti-resurrection core. PR #19 covers versioning. Issue #22, from Ilan Strauss on 2026-10-22, proposes an `applies_to` field and an agentic-coding conformance profile.
title: Proposals under review

# Ilan Strauss

Ilan is an economist. He co-directs the [AI Disclosures Project](../project/ai-disclosures-project.md) with Tim O’Reilly and co-writes [Asimov’s Addendum](../blog/asimovs-addendum.md). Before answering him, check [how he likes to be addressed](communication.md). His work: [papers](papers.md), [affiliations](affiliations.md) and [his part in OMP](omp-work.md).

# Ilan’s affiliations

Besides co-directing the project, Ilan is an honorary senior fellow at UCL’s Institute for Innovation and Public Purpose, a senior fellow at the Microsoft AI Economy Institute, a visiting associate professor at the University of Johannesburg, and on the editorial board of Data & Policy. Profile: [Ilan Strauss](ilan.md).
title: Ilan’s affiliations

body:
# Ilan’s papers

Ilan wrote “‘Rich-get-richer’? Platform Attention and Earnings Inequality” with Jangho Yang and Mariana Mazzucato (Industrial and Corporate Change, July 2026), and “M&A as Capability Building” with Jangho Yang (Applied Economics Letters, April 2026). With Tim O’Reilly and M. Moure he wrote [Protocols and Power](../research/protocols-and-power.md); with Sruly Rosenblat, O’Reilly and others, [MCP in practice](../research/mcp-in-practice.md) and [the attribution work](../research/attribution-and-access.md).
title: Ilan’s papers

body:
# Ilan’s part in the Open Memory Protocol

Ilan co-wrote the ecosystem scoping note with Sruly Rosenblat, one of the drafts the v0.2 spec combines. He proposed a thin core with separately versioned semantic conventions (issue I-21 in [the open issues](../spec/open-issues.md)). On 2026-10-22 he opened issue #22, proposing an `applies_to` field and an agentic-coding conformance profile ([proposals](../spec/open-prs.md)).
title: Ilan’s part in the Open Memory Protocol
